on_unmapped_default: warn+skip — a slicer column that resolves to no master column is DROPPED loudly (never silently wired to the wrong column, never shipped dead)
description: Power BI interaction -> Sigma control kind. Basic list/date slicers are emitted mechanically. Native drill and legend controls are emitted only when source hierarchy/color bindings prove every source and target column; unresolved or unsupported mappings remain surfaced gaps because an unattached control is dead UI.

rows.notes: Categorical list control (documented default): controlType:list + mode:include + selectionMode:multiple + source{kind:source,...} + filters[]. A slicer bound to a date column is overridden to date-range in code.

Date/datetime-typed slicer: controlType:date-range + mode:between + includeNulls. Needs NO source (columns come from filters[]) but DOES require the flat mode or the POST 400s 'Invalid kind: control'.

Native hierarchy control is the released target when every hierarchy field and filter target is known. Current PBIR extraction often exposes only the active projection, so the builder keeps the active level and records the missing hierarchy rather than inventing columns.

A proven Category/Axis hierarchy emits a native drill control. The active projection remains the chart axis; the full ordered hierarchy maps to categories and target columnIds. Every level must resolve on both the page master and target chart or the converter records a loud gap and emits no dead control.

A visible categorical Legend/Series binding on a supported chart emits a native legend control sourced from the page master and targeted to the chart color column; the chart-local duplicate is hidden. Power BI legend.show=false remains chart formatting and emits no control. Sigma legend controls do not support waterfall, whose splitBy legend remains chart-local.
